text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Tuesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Culture Minister Rihards Piks decided to resign following the conclusion by the prosecutor's office that he had breached the anti-corruption law. A spokesman for prime minister Andris Shkele said the resignation would be accepted.

- Prime Minister Shkele will go on TV this morning to speak about the political situation in the country. A spokesman said the premier would not announce his resignation over the anti-corruption scandal.
- Around 20 former workers of the Riga chinaware factory, most of them women, announced a hunger-strike to protest against wage arrears and non-payment of social tax by the plant.
- Leading party Latvia's Way is against plans to increase MPs salaries.
- Juris Matusevics, 19, became the first Latvian admitted to the West Point military academy.
- Latvia's foreign trade deficit has been going down gradually in the first quarter of the year.
- Coopers & Lybrands is investigating the deals by the former president of the Latvian Shipping company, Peteris Avotins, at the request of the privatisation agency.
- Parliament's committee for mandates and inquiries has decided to ask for 46 MPs to be investigated by the general prosecutor's if they breached the anti-corruption law.

- Most Latvian officials whom a Chechen parliamentary delegation met yesterday showed reluctance to establish official contacts. The delegation may have problems with entering Estonia since its members have only ex-Soviet interior passports which the country no longer recognises.
